verdict.rationale: Anytype's source is publicly viewable on GitHub (anytype-gh-1, anytype-gh-2) and some components are labeled 'open-source' (anytype-docs-35), suggesting readable source. However, community evidence directly contradicts an 'open license' claim: commenters note Anytype uses a 'source-available license' that 'doesn't match the popular Open Source Definition' (anytype-comm-12, anytype-comm-15), meaning the source is visible but not under a recognized open-source license as an AI-native user might expect. missing for 10: a first-party license statement (e.g., LICENSE file terms), clarification of which repos/components are truly OSI-licensed vs source-available, and resolution of the community dispute.
